Now I see the issue clearly. In the `null_terminated = true` case (which is the default for `read_json`), the code does `std::memcpy(&c, it, 5)` reading 5 bytes without checking if there are at least 5 bytes available. The comment says "because our buffer must be null terminated, we can read one more index without checking" - but this is wrong because it reads 5 bytes, not just one more.

If the input is just `"t\0"` (2 bytes), then `std::memcpy(&c, it, 5)` reads 5 bytes starting from `it`, which is 3 bytes past the end of the 2-byte buffer. This is a container-overflow READ.

But wait, let me check the `check_is_padded` condition. The `if constexpr (not check_is_padded(Opts))` check at line 529 checks if `size_t(end - it) < 4`. If the buffer has fewer than 4 bytes remaining, it returns an error. So for a buffer of `{'t', '\0'}` (2 bytes), `end - it = 2 < 4`, so it would return an error before reaching the `std::memcpy`.
